unit.title: Pricing
unit.description: Cost-plus, value-based, skimming, penetration, psychological prices, elasticity, decoy, good-better-best, margin and break-even

cards.definition: Setting the price by adding a margin to the unit cost. Simple and safe for costs, but it ignores what customers are willing to pay and what competitors charge.
cards.example: A craftsman who adds 40 percent to the cost of materials and labour.

cards.definition: The maximum price a customer would pay for an offer. It depends on perceived value and on alternatives, not on your costs; it is measured with surveys, tests and sales data.
cards.example: Asking at which price a product becomes too expensive and at which it looks suspiciously cheap (Van Westendorp method).

cards.definition: Offering several versions at rising prices (Basic, Pro, Business) so each customer picks the level that fits; the middle tier is often the target and the top tier makes it look reasonable.
cards.example: A software sold 9, 29 and 99 euros per month, with most customers choosing 29.

cards.definition: Frequent discounts train customers to wait for the next sale, lower the reference price in their minds and erode margins. Promotions should have a clear goal and an end.
cards.example: A clothing brand always at minus 30 percent: nobody buys at full price any more.

cards.definition: Margin is profit divided by the selling price; markup is profit divided by the cost. Buying at 60 and selling at 100 gives a 40 percent margin but a 67 percent markup.
cards.example: Confusing the two in a negotiation can make you sell at a loss without noticing.

exercises.prompt: Which pricing method starts from what customers are ready to pay?
choices: Value-based pricing
Cost-plus pricing
Copying the competitor price
Penetration pricing
exercises.explain: Value-based pricing captures the value perceived by the customer. Costs set the floor, not the price.

exercises.prompt: A new console launches at 549 euros, then drops in price each year. Which strategy?
choices: Price skimming
Penetration pricing
Charm pricing
Cost-plus pricing
exercises.explain: Skimming takes the high-willingness buyers first (fans, early adopters), then lowers the price to reach the mass market.

exercises.prompt: A new streaming service launches at 1 euro a month to win users fast. Which strategy?
choices: Penetration pricing
Price skimming
Prestige pricing
Value-based pricing
exercises.explain: Penetration pricing buys market share fast. It works when scale lowers costs or when customers stay after the price rises.

exercises.prompt: Why is 19.99 euros often used instead of 20 euros?
choices: Buyers read the first digit and feel it is in the tens
The law forbids round prices in shops
It lowers the VAT paid by the shop
Card terminals process it faster
exercises.explain: Charm pricing plays on left-digit reading. Luxury brands do the opposite: round prices signal quality.

exercises.prompt: You raise a price by 10 percent and sales fall by 30 percent. What does it say about demand?
choices: It is very elastic: buyers are sensitive to price
It is inelastic: buyers do not care about price
Elasticity cannot be computed from these figures
Revenue went up because the price went up
exercises.explain: Elasticity = minus 30 divided by plus 10 = minus 3. Revenue falls: 1.10 times 0.70 = 0.77 of the original.

exercises.prompt: Popcorn: small 5 euros, medium 7.50 euros, large 8 euros. What is the medium for?
choices: It is a decoy that makes the large look like a bargain
It is the most profitable option for the cinema
The law requires three sizes in a cinema
It is there for people who cannot choose
exercises.explain: The decoy effect: a poor option placed near the target pushes buyers toward it. Who would take the medium for only 50 cents less?

exercises.prompt: A software sells three plans: 9, 29 and 99 euros. What is the main role of the 99 euro plan?
choices: Serve big accounts and make 29 euros look reasonable
Be the plan most customers choose in the end
Lower the average price paid per customer
Replace the need for a free trial
exercises.explain: Good, better, best: the top tier captures customers with high willingness to pay and anchors the middle tier, usually the target.

exercises.prompt: You buy a product 60 euros and sell it 100 euros. What is your margin rate?
choices: 40 percent
67 percent
60 percent
100 percent
exercises.explain: Margin = 40 divided by the selling price 100. The markup, 40 divided by the cost 60, is 67 percent: do not confuse them.

exercises.prompt: Fixed costs: 20,000 euros. Each unit sold leaves 40 euros after variable costs. How many units to break even?
exercises.explain: Break-even = fixed costs divided by unit contribution: 20,000 divided by 40 = 500 units. Beyond that, each sale is profit.

exercises.prompt: Running a promotion every month is a reliable way to grow a brand over the long term.
exercises.explain: False. Constant discounts lower the reference price, train customers to wait and squeeze margins. Promotions need a goal and an end date.

exercises.prompt: Which method sets a price without knowing the willingness to pay of customers?
choices: Cost-plus pricing
Value-based pricing
A Van Westendorp survey
A price test on two groups
exercises.explain: Cost-plus looks only inward. It protects the margin on paper but can leave money on the table or price you out of the market.

exercises.title: Pricing a new online course
exercises.scenario: You launch an online course on digital marketing for freelancers. Production cost: 6,000 euros. Competitors sell between 99 and 499 euros.

steps.prompt: How do you start setting the price?
choices: Interview freelancers about value and alternatives
Divide 6,000 euros by the sales you hope for
Take the cheapest competitor price minus 10 percent
Pick 497 euros because it ends with a 7
steps.feedback: Willingness to pay comes first. Costs tell you the minimum, competitors tell you the frame, customers tell you the value.

steps.prompt: Interviews show freelancers want a result: their first two clients. How do you structure the offer?
choices: Three tiers: course only, course plus group calls, course plus 1 to 1 review
One single price for everyone, to keep things simple
A free course and paid ads inside the videos
The course only, with a permanent 50 percent discount
steps.feedback: Good, better, best tiers let each buyer pick the level of help they value; the coaching tiers carry most of the margin.

steps.prompt: Launch week: how do you use a promotion without damaging the price?
choices: A launch price for 7 days, clearly dated, then the normal price
A discount that renews every Monday with a timer
A fake crossed-out price that never existed
No price shown at all: contact us for a quote
steps.feedback: A real, dated launch offer rewards early buyers. A fake reference price is a misleading commercial practice in France.

exercises.explain: Value first, tiers to capture different willingness to pay, honest promotions with a clear end.
